source.title: SAMPLE COSTS TO ESTABLISH AND PRODUCE
source.publisher: UC Davis Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics / UC Cooperative Extension

priceYear.quote: The sample costs for labor, materials, equipment and custom services are based on January 2018 figures.

acresFarmed.quote: The hypothetical farm consists of 500 contiguous acres.

interestRatePct.quote: An interest rate of 5.5 percent is used to calculate capital recovery.

operatingInterestRatePct.quote: Interest on operating capital is based on cash operating costs and is calculated monthly until harvest at a nominal rate of 5.0 percent per year.

laborMachineRate.quote: Hourly wages for workers are $13.00 for machine operators and $11.00 per hour non-machine labor.

laborNonMachineRate.quote: Hourly wages for workers are $13.00 for machine operators and $11.00 per hour non-machine labor.

laborOverheadPct.quote: Management salaries include annual bonuses, and insurance, payroll taxes and benefits which are calculated at 40.5 percent.

yieldStatement.quote: For this analysis, selected yields ranged from 850 to 1,750 boxes per acre and crop prices ranged from $12.50 to $21.50 per box.

priceStatement.quote: Based on grower and cooperator information, an estimated price of $17 per box for Sheegene-21 grapes is used in this analysis.

costsPerAcre.title: COSTS PER ACRE TO PRODUCE TABLE GRAPES Sheegene-21

capitalRecoveryFormula.quote: The formula for the calculation of the annual capital recovery costs is; ((Purchase Price – Salvage Value) x Capital Recovery Factor) + (Salvage Value x Interest Rate).

salvageMethod.quote: Salvage value is an estimate of the remaining value of an investment at the end of its useful life.

propertyTaxRatePct.quote: County taxes are calculated as 1 percent of the average value of the property.

machineLaborFactor.quote: Labor for operations involving machinery are 20 percent higher than the operation time given in Table 2 to account for the extra labor involved in equipment set up, moving, maintenance, work breaks, and field repair.

removalCost.note: Removal of the previous planting, charged as a pre-plant cost in the first establishment year. The studies do not charge an end-of-life removal and set the establishment asset salvage value to zero.
